cohort: The study included 280 women from 13 public hospitals in eastern Ethiopia, comprising 70 cases who died during pregnancy, childbirth, or postpartum within 42 days of termination, and 210 controls who survived severe obstetric complications.
finding: The primary finding was that maternal mortality was significantly associated with caesarean section, admission to an intensive care unit, postpartum hemorrhage, and pre-existing medical conditions.
mod_finding: Women who died were significantly more likely to have given birth by caesarean section (aOR = 3.35).
